title: Minimum percentage gain
statement: The current general five-pillars baseline requires a stock to already be up at least 10% on the session.

evidence.title: How To Start Day Trading in 2026 (full training)
evidence.note: The current full training lists at least 10% gain as a five-pillars requirement.

title: Relative volume floor
statement: The current general five-pillars baseline requires relative volume of at least 5x normal volume; higher is preferred.

evidence.title: How To Start Day Trading in 2026 (full training)
evidence.note: The current full training requires five-times relative volume and explains the reference as average daily volume over the prior 50 days.

title: Core price band
statement: The current general strategy focuses on $2-$20 stocks, with roughly $5-$10 described as an especially attractive range.

evidence.title: How To Start Day Trading in 2026 (full training)
evidence.note: The current full training defines $2-$20 as a pillar and $5-$10 as a preferred sweet spot.

title: Low-float supply constraint
statement: The current general five-pillars baseline prefers float below 10 million shares, with lower generally better.

evidence.title: How To Start Day Trading in 2026 (full training)
evidence.note: The current full training lists float below 10M shares as the fifth pillar.

title: Fresh catalyst for A-quality
statement: Fresh company news is part of the current A-quality five-pillars screen. A no-news stock may be considered conditionally when it becomes the unmistakable market leader, but that is an exception rather than A-quality.

evidence.title: How To Start Day Trading in 2026 (full training)
evidence.note: Current training says news is required for A-quality while sector-wide catalysts are riskier exceptions.

title: High total volume is an extra preference
statement: High total volume improves tradability and is strongly preferred, but it is not one of the canonical five pillars in the current full-training definition.

evidence.title: How To Start Day Trading in 2026 (full training)
evidence.note: The full training distinguishes high total volume from relative volume and says performance improves with higher total volume.

title: Stricter small-account screen
statement: The January 2026 small-account challenge intentionally tightened the general strategy toward roughly $1.50-$6, at least 25% gain, at least 5x RVOL, float under 10M, and top-three gainer status.

evidence.title: I Reset My Account to $2,000 (AGAIN) Robinhood Challenge Ep 1
evidence.note: The challenge plan explicitly tightens price, gain, float and top-gainer rank while keeping RVOL at 5x.

title: Attention leader preference
statement: Prefer the stock where market attention is concentrated, especially the leading percentage gainer; obviousness is a cross-sectional state rather than a chart pattern.

evidence.title: I Reset My Account to $2,000 (AGAIN) Robinhood Challenge Ep 1
evidence.note: The small-account plan explicitly wants top-three percentage gainers.

title: Morning trading window
statement: The current baseline focuses new entries from 7:00 a.m. to about 10:00 a.m. Eastern, including premarket.

evidence.title: I Reset My Account to $2,000 (AGAIN) Robinhood Challenge Ep 1
evidence.note: The 2026 challenge plan specifies 7 a.m.-10 a.m. Eastern.

title: MACD settings
statement: The MACD used in the current methodology uses standard 12/26/9 settings with close as the source.

evidence.title: How to Read Technical Indicators on Candlestick Charts
evidence.note: The technical-indicator class explicitly shows MACD inputs 12, 26, 9 with close as source and advises not changing them.

title: Front-side momentum
statement: Long setups are preferred on the front side while MACD is positive; after MACD turns negative the baseline waits, and a later positive MACD near the high can represent a reclaim.

evidence.title: This Stock Dropped 97% in 12hrs...
evidence.note: Ross explicitly uses one-minute MACD to distinguish front side from back side and waits for a return to positive before reconsidering.
